members.title: US Congress approves Russia sanctions that impact China and India
members.description: US lawmakers have approved sweeping new sanctions targeting Russia's economy and Putin's inner circle, with Trump set to sign a bill that also threatens steep tariffs on major buyers of Russian oil, including China and India.

members.title: US senator's 'clean up your act' warning to India, China over Russia
members.description: The US Congress has passed legislation that could impose tariffs of up to 100% on goods from countries buying Russian energy, sending President Donald Trump a sanctions package aimed at reducing Moscow's revenues and divided Democrats over the scope of his trade powers. The House of Representatives approved the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 by 262-159 on Wednesday.

members.title: Scientists develop new method for deciphering ancient scrolls
members.description: Even a handheld XRF scanner is sufficient to determine most promising scrolls for further analysis.

members.title: Hidden “immune organ” in the skull may help fight brain cancer
members.description: Scientists discovered a hidden “immune organ” inside the skull that acts as a rapid first responder against brain cancer in mice. Strengthening this local immune defense improved tumor rejection and survival, raising the possibility of new treatments that target the skull directly.

members.title: Scientists find an immune “false alarm” that may drive rapid aging
members.description: Scientists have discovered that some severe genetic disorders linked to rapid aging may be driven not just by damaged DNA, but by the body’s overreaction to that damage. When broken DNA fragments leak into the wrong part of a cell, an immune sensor called cGAS can mistake them for signs of a viral infection, triggering chronic inflammation and even interfering with DNA repair itself.

members.title: Scientists recreated what mice saw from brain activity alone
members.description: Scientists reconstructed videos from the brain activity of mice, producing 10-second clips based only on signals from neurons in the visual cortex. The breakthrough could help reveal how the brain reshapes what we see before it becomes our perception of reality.

members.title: STAT+: Scientists made mice with half a brain. Then they filled them with human organoids
members.description: Scientists have made mice with half a brain, then filled them with human organoids — possibly opening new avenues for research but also raising ethical issues.

members.title: Scientists turn seawater into fresh water without harmful brine
members.description: Scientists have developed a solar-powered desalination system that turns seawater into fresh water while removing nearly all of the leftover salt as a solid instead of producing harmful brine. The self-cleaning technology could also recover valuable minerals such as lithium, potentially turning desalination waste into a useful resource.
